about: Math spans the workspace's Markdown parser must find: each case's math tokens in document order, as [type, content, info]. The rules are mdit-py-plugins 0.6.1's dollarmath with allow_labels=True, allow_space=False, allow_digits=True, allow_blank_lines=False and double_inline=True, on markdown-it's default preset (markdown-it-py: js-default) with html off, plus one rule of this project's own: a $$ block ends within 200 lines of its opening line. Cases marked with that rule give other spans with the plugin alone; the plugin gives all the others. Code spans are markdown-it 15's, which the browser runs: the server ports its rule, since markdown-it-py 4.2 keeps markdown-it 14's (cases marked markdown_it_15_code_spans). The server's parser must pass every case.

cases.name: no blank lines in a block
block quote, whose markers the content keeps (the original's quirk)
a backslash ending the text escapes a dollar starting it (the original's quirk)
non-ASCII whitespace ends a text: a final backslash escapes the first dollar
non-ASCII whitespace starts a text: a final backslash escapes the first dollar
the end's step back counts code points (the original's quirk)
the end's step back counts code points, at the start of a line
a line that starts and ends with $$ is one block (the original's quirk)
a block can end in the next list item (the original's quirk)
a block can end 200 lines after its opening line
